findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "find" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "how_roblox" appears informational but accepts parameters (history) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: action, q, topic, id, since, history

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: person, routine, posts · Private data: page_cards, my_games, my_game_numbers, track · Public sink: genres, my_game_numbers, my_game_days, routine · Destructive: person, track, routine.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: person, routine, posts · Private data: page_cards, my_games, my_game_numbers, track · Public sink: genres, my_game_numbers, my_game_days, routine · Destructive: person, track, routine

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "studio" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

With studio instead: the studio’s whole page, as RoBot"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
